title: Screams, scares and suspense as Paranormal Activity arrives in Norwich
excerpt: There were plenty of screams, gasps and people jumping in their seats as Paranormal Activity brought a night of supernatural suspense to Norwich Theatre Royal.
content:
There were plenty of screams, gasps and people jumping in their seats as Paranormal Activity brought a night of supernatural suspense to Norwich Theatre Royal.

The production does a brilliant job of building tension, steadily drawing the audience into its chilling story before delivering a series of unexpected scares.

Set inside a cleverly designed house, complete with an upstairs and downstairs, the staging makes you feel as though you are right there alongside the characters as increasingly unsettling events unfold.

The set featured the use of Facetime and Alexa (Image: Johan Persson)

James Bye, best known for playing Martin Fowler in EastEnders for more than 10 years, stars as James.

His character is friendly, lovable and an instant hit, providing a likeable presence as the horror begins to take hold.

James Bye, played James in the production (Image: Johan Persson)

Hannah Sinclair Robinson plays his wife, Lou, delivering an incredible performance throughout.

She captures her character’s emotions and growing fear exceptionally well, making the increasingly disturbing events feel all the more real.

Jo Castleton, as Etheline Cotgrave, brings the supernatural activity to life with a series of cinematic scares, while Caroline Faber plays James’s mother, Carolanne – an overbearing but full-of-life character who brings plenty of personality to the household.

The lighting and sound created an uncomfortable suspense which added to the performance (Image: Johan Persson)

One of the production’s greatest strengths is its ability to keep the audience guessing.

There were moments when a jump scare seemed inevitable, only for nothing to happen, while others came completely unexpectedly.

The creative team deserves huge credit for the way it manages to create such convincing horrors on stage.

How some of the effects are achieved remains a mystery and I found myself trying to work it out on the drive home.

The set and costumes were integral into the illusions of the performance (Image: Johan Persson)

With clever staging, brilliant performances and suspense that keeps you on edge, Paranormal Activity is a thoroughly entertaining production that will leave you thinking twice about what might be lurking in the dark.

The show is running until November 14 at Norwich Theatre Royal.
